h1: The 6 Best Dehumidifiers With Pumps of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Dehumidifiers With Pumps: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 6 dehumidifiers with built-in pumps scored on drainage options, coverage, noise and smart controls, priced $100 to $500.
summary: The hOmeLabs 50 pint dehumidifier is the best pump model for a large, damp basement, with 7,500 square feet of listed coverage and Wi-Fi control. The Midea 50 pint is the quieter, simpler alternative that pumps vertically or horizontally. The GE is built for below-grade basements, and the AEOCKY pushes water up to 16.5 feet.
intro: The built-in pump is the feature that decides whether a basement dehumidifier is a convenience or a chore. Without one, you empty a bucket daily or run a hose that depends on gravity, which fails the moment the drain is above the unit. A pump removes that limit, but it brings a new one: how far and how high it can push, which most listings barely mention.

Primea editors reviewed six dehumidifiers that state a built-in pump and ranked them on drainage options, stated coverage, noise, smart controls and how well each suits a below-grade space. We excluded models that mention a pump nowhere in their listing, and counted the two Midea listings as one model since they share a name.

products.name: hOmeLabs 50 Pint Dehumidifier with Pump (7,500 Sq Ft)
products.verdict: 7,500 square feet of listed coverage, a built-in pump and Wi-Fi control.
products.description:
The hOmeLabs unit is rated for 7,500 square feet at 50 pints, has a versatile built-in pump and is Wi-Fi enabled, so you can adjust humidity from your phone. Remote control matters in a basement, where you do not want to walk downstairs to check a reading.

It wins because it lists the largest coverage of the group and pairs the pump with app control. The Midea below is quieter and simpler, but the hOmeLabs suits big open basements better.

Buy it for a large, damp space. Cost is the drawback at $200 to $500, and with no noise figure listed, expect a typical dehumidifier hum.
products.idealFor: Large open basements that need strong, remote-controlled drying.
products.skipIf: You want a quiet bedroom or small-room unit.

products.name: Midea 50 Pint Dehumidifier with Pump
products.verdict: A pump that drains vertically or horizontally, at 49 dBA on low.
products.description:
Midea's 50 pint unit lists 4,500 square feet of coverage, a built-in water pump that drains vertically or horizontally, and quiet operation at 49 dBA in low mode. The vertical option is the one you need for a drain higher than the unit.

It ranks second because the hOmeLabs covers more area and adds Wi-Fi, while the Midea gives a measured noise figure. Compared with the GE below, it states coverage and sound, which makes it easier to judge.

A strong match for a finished basement or utility room. The caveat is that 4,500 square feet is the ceiling, so very large spaces call for the hOmeLabs.
products.idealFor: Finished basements and utility rooms where noise matters.
products.skipIf: Your space is larger than 4,500 square feet.

products.name: GE Dehumidifier with Pump & Hose
products.verdict: Built for below-grade basements, with Smart Dry fan control and continuous drain.
products.description:
The GE lists a built-in pump for below-grade basements, a Smart Dry mode that adjusts fan speed based on the room, and an easy-to-empty tank or continuous drain. Smart Dry slows the fan when humidity is near target, which saves energy.

It ranks third because it names the below-grade use case directly but gives no coverage, noise or capacity figures. The brand is the draw: GE parts and service are easy to find.

A good pick for a below-grade basement. The caveat is that the missing specs mean you should confirm capacity and coverage on the product page.
cons: No coverage or pint figure here
products.idealFor: Below-grade basements where the drain sits above the unit.
products.skipIf: You want listed coverage and noise numbers.

products.name: AEOCKY Dehumidifier with Pump (Up to 16.5 ft)
products.verdict: A pump rated for up to 16.5 feet, with an Energy Star Most Efficient badge.
products.description:
AEOCKY's flagship, the LEO-001, lists a pump rated for up to 16.5 feet and carries an Energy Star Most Efficient 2025 label. Pump lift is the number that matters when the drain is above the unit.

It ranks fourth because the pump reach is a rare, concrete figure, but the listing otherwise reads as marketing and gives no coverage or capacity. It sits above the Gasbye for the stated lift and efficiency rating.

Choose it when the drain is far away or high. The caveat is that the listing's competitive claims should be read skeptically until you check the capacity on the product page.
products.idealFor: Basements where the drain is high or far from the unit.
products.skipIf: You want a long-established appliance brand.

products.name: Gasbye Energy Star Dehumidifier with Pump
products.verdict: Energy Star rated, with a 44 dB quiet pump drainage system for basements.
products.description:
The Gasbye is an Energy Star dehumidifier for basements with a pump and a 44 dB quiet pump drainage. Pump noise is a separate problem from compressor noise, since a gurgling pump kicks in at random.

It ranks fifth because 44 dB is the quietest figure in the group, but the listing leaves out coverage and capacity. It beats the avylo below on specifics but trails the Midea for describing the pump's directions.

A fit for a finished basement near living space. The caveat is that the improved-performance claim has no baseline in the listing.
products.idealFor: Finished basements where noise is the main complaint.
products.skipIf: You want a published coverage rating.

products.name: avylo Dehumidifier for Basement with Pump and Hose
products.verdict: Three drainage options and intelligent humidity control for basements.
products.description:
avylo sells a basement dehumidifier with pump and hose, three drainage options and intelligent humidity control. Three drain modes, usually tank, gravity hose and pump, let it adapt to a changing setup.

It ranks last because the listing is the thinnest here: energy-efficient performance is claimed without a figure, and there is no coverage, noise or lift. It earns its place by clearly covering the drain flexibility that this category depends on.

A workable choice if drain options matter most. The caveat is that every performance claim needs verification on the product page.
cons: No numbers for coverage or noise
products.idealFor: Basements where the drain setup may change.
products.skipIf: You need measured specs to compare.

whatMatters.detail: Lift is how high the pump pushes water, and it decides whether you can drain into a sink or standpipe above the unit. AEOCKY lists up to 16.5 feet. Check the listing for lift, not just the word pump, and measure the height of your drain before choosing.

Pint rating shows how much moisture the unit removes per day, and coverage shows the space it can handle. The hOmeLabs lists 7,500 square feet, the Midea 4,500. Match the figure to your space, and size up for very damp areas, because an undersized unit runs constantly.

Dehumidifiers run for hours, so decibels matter in a living space. The Gasbye lists 44 dB on its pump and the Midea 49 dBA on low. Check whether the figure refers to the fan, the compressor or the pump, since each is different, and remember a pump that cycles on intermittently is more noticeable than steady fan noise.

A good unit offers a tank, a gravity hose and a pump. The GE and avylo list tank or continuous options. Check for a hose in the box and look at the connector type, because mismatched fittings are a common setup problem, and a short supplied hose may force you to buy an extension.

Wi-Fi control and fan automation let you manage humidity without visiting the basement. The hOmeLabs adds Wi-Fi and the GE has Smart Dry. Check the listing for app support and a humidity readout, since remote control with no sensor feedback is of little use.

cards.text: Pushes water up and across to a distant drain. The Midea, AEOCKY and GE list built-in pumps.

cards.label: Gravity hose
cards.text: Needs the drain lower than the unit and has no moving parts. Models like the avylo offer this as one of three options.

howToChoose.note: Choose a pump when your drain is above the unit or far away.

cards.text: A pump with stated lift, a coverage rating above your floor area and continuous drain. These decide whether you ever touch the unit.

cards.text: You have a large or very damp space. The hOmeLabs or AEOCKY in the $200 to $500 tier add coverage and lift.

faq.q: Do I need a pump on my dehumidifier?
faq.a: If your drain is above the unit or far away, yes. The Midea pumps vertically or horizontally, and the AEOCKY lists up to 16.5 feet of lift. If a floor drain is nearby, a gravity hose is enough.

faq.q: What mistake do buyers make with pump dehumidifiers?
faq.a: Assuming the pump handles any distance. Check the lift figure on the listing, such as the AEOCKY's 16.5 feet, and measure your drain height before ordering. A weak pump leaves water in the line.

faq.q: Is the hOmeLabs worth it over the Midea?
faq.a: For a large basement, yes. The hOmeLabs lists 7,500 square feet and Wi-Fi control, while the Midea lists 4,500 square feet and a 49 dBA low setting. Choose the Midea for a smaller, quieter space.

faq.q: How do I set up the pump?
faq.a: Attach the hose to the pump outlet, run it to your drain with a steady upward or downward slope, and secure the end. The GE and avylo ship with hoses, but check the fitting size before connecting.

faq.q: How do I maintain a dehumidifier?
faq.a: Clean the filter monthly and check the hose for kinks or algae. On the Gasbye or GE, rinse the tank if you use it instead of the pump, and flush the pump line if the water turns cloudy.

faq.q: Can I use a dehumidifier in winter?
faq.a: Some drop in performance in cold rooms because coils frost. Check the listed operating temperature on the product page, and note that the hOmeLabs listing cites a 95 degree rating. Heated basements run best.

finalTake: The hOmeLabs 50 pint dehumidifier is the pump model to buy for a large basement, thanks to its 7,500 square feet of coverage and Wi-Fi control. The Midea is the quieter, simpler choice with a flexible pump, and the GE suits below-grade spaces. Choose the AEOCKY when your drain sits high, and the Gasbye when noise is the problem.
